lines: I know what happened at the {stolen_container}. <aqua>{theft_witness_possessive}</aqua> story reached me.
The {stolen_container} has been part of more conversations since you touched it.
<aqua>{theft_witness}</aqua> saw enough at the {stolen_container} for the village to remember.
Word travels quickly when someone reaches where they should not.
I have heard about the {stolen_stack}. That makes this greeting colder than it might have been.
The village is small. A hand in the wrong {stolen_container} does not stay secret.
You arrive with a story already attached to you.
I know enough about the theft to keep my distance.
A greeting is all I am offering while that {stolen_container} is still in memory.
People are still talking about what happened. I am one of them.
I heard <aqua>{theft_witness_possessive}</aqua> account of the {stolen_container}.
You should know the village is talking about what went missing.
This is a difficult place to ask for welcome after opening someone else's container.
The owner has counted the loss and named what you took.
People who once left their doors open are locking them now.
You may want to return the goods before starting any other conversation.
The guards have heard the same story I did.
A greeting feels dishonest when theft is standing between us.
I am willing to listen, but not to pretend nothing happened.
Settle the matter at the {stolen_container}, then come back.
